questions.stem: A Category 1 compounded sterile preparation is made in a hood in an unclassified area. Can it get a 4-day beyond-use date?

options.text: No; the maximum is 12 hours at room temperature or 24 hours refrigerated

questions.explanation: C is correct: Category 1 maxes out at 12 hours at room temperature or 24 hours refrigerated. A and B go beyond those limits. D is wrong because Category 1 has no 4-day frozen option.

questions.stem: What is the maximum refrigerated beyond-use date for a Category 1 preparation?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Category 1 is up to 24 hours refrigerated. A, 12 hours, is the room-temperature limit. C and B are Category 2 example dates.

questions.stem: A Category 2 preparation is made aseptically from sterile ingredients, with no sterility test, and stored in the refrigerator. What is the beyond-use date?
questions.explanation: C is correct: this common Category 2 example is 4 days at room temperature or 10 days in the fridge. A is the Category 1 refrigerated limit. B is the room-temperature date. D is far longer than the 10-day refrigerated date for this example.

questions.stem: Which category allows the longest beyond-use dates?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Category 3 adds extra testing for the longest dates. A has the shortest dates. B is in between. D is wrong because the dates differ by category.

questions.stem: What pressure should a room for compounding hazardous drugs have?
questions.explanation: A is correct: negative pressure keeps hazardous drug particles from leaking out into the pharmacy. B, positive pressure, pushes air out and is used to keep germs away from sterile work. C and D do not contain the drug.

questions.stem: A pharmacist compounds a hazardous chemotherapy drug. Which protections apply? Select all that apply.

options.text: A hood vented to the outside

questions.explanation: B, C, D, and E are correct: two pairs of chemotherapy-tested gloves, a protective gown, a negative pressure room, and a hood vented to the outside. A is wrong because positive pressure would push drug particles out.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the purpose of USP chapter 800?

options.text: It protects the worker from hazardous drugs
It sets beyond-use dates for sterile preparations
It protects the patient from germs

questions.explanation: A is correct: chapter 800 protects the worker. B and D describe chapter 797, which protects the patient and sets sterile beyond-use dates. C is wrong because chapter 800 covers hazardous drugs.

questions.stem: Who sets the beyond-use date on a compounded preparation?
questions.explanation: B is correct: the beyond-use date is set by the compounder for the preparation they made. A, the manufacturer, sets the expiration date for the original product. C and D do not set dating.

questions.stem: Sterile compounding work happens inside which environment?
questions.explanation: A is correct: sterile work happens inside a hood with very clean air, International Organization for Standardization Class 5. B, C, and D lack the clean air the chapter requires.

questions.stem: Which statements about USP chapter 797 are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Category 2 preparations are made in a cleanroom suite
Category 1 maxes out at 12 hours at room temperature
A common Category 2 example lasts 4 days at room temperature
Category 1 can get 10 days in the refrigerator

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and E are correct: Category 2 is made in a cleanroom suite, Category 1 maxes out at 12 hours at room temperature, a common Category 2 example lasts 4 days at room temperature, and chapter 797 protects the patient. D is wrong because Category 1 maxes out at 24 hours refrigerated.
